subs.label: Korean Drama
subs.axis: Axis: by the genre the Korean industry and fandom name: romance forms first (rom-com, office, chaebol, melodrama), then the serial forms (makjang, revenge, family), the historical sageuk, professional and thriller genres, fantasy romance, and school and youth drama last

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy (rom-com)
leaves.defn: A Korean romance series whose engine is comic: mismatched leads, a contrived premise that forces them together, and a happy ending (Coffee Prince, Because This Is My First Life, Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha). A romance set mainly at work goes to B2-2; a rich-heir and poor-heroine romance goes to B2-3; a supernatural premise goes to B2-12.
leaves.see: B2-2 Office Romance; B2-3 Chaebol Romance; B2-12 Fantasy Romance
leaves.axis: by the premise that throws the couple together: contract and fake relationships first, then cohabitation, disguise, showbiz, mature second chances, small-town healing; genre-hybrid rom-coms last

leaves.label: Office Romance
leaves.defn: A Korean romance series set inside a workplace, where the job, hierarchy and colleagues drive the love story (What's Wrong with Secretary Kim, Business Proposal, Pasta, Romance Is a Bonus Book). A series about a profession first and foremost (hospital, court) goes to B2-9 or B2-10.
leaves.see: B2-1 Romantic Comedy; B2-9 Medical Drama; B2-10 Legal Drama
leaves.axis: by the workplace: boss-and-secretary hierarchies first, then company ensembles, kitchens and shops, media and creative industries

leaves.label: Chaebol Romance
leaves.defn: A Korean romance built on the class gap between a chaebol (conglomerate) heir or heiress and a poor partner, the "Candy" Cinderella formula (Boys over Flowers, Lovers in Paris, The Heirs, Queen of Tears). Chaebol family intrigue with birth secrets and revenge goes to B2-5 Makjang.
leaves.aliases: Cinderella story; Candy-girl romance; jaebeol romance
leaves.see: B2-1 Romantic Comedy; B2-5 Makjang Drama
leaves.axis: by who is rich: the Cinderella form (poor heroine, rich heir) first, then the reverse (heiress and poor man), then royals of an imagined constitutional monarchy

leaves.label: Korean Melodrama
leaves.defn: A Korean romance played for tears or emotional realism rather than laughs: fated or doomed love, illness, love triangles, adultery, or the quiet realism of adult relationships (Winter Sonata, Autumn in My Heart, Something in the Rain, Secret Love Affair). Melodrama of birth secrets, affairs and outrageous plotting goes to B2-5 Makjang.
leaves.see: B2-5 Makjang Drama; B2-1 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by emotional mode, in the order the forms arose: early trendy dramas first, then Hallyu tearjerkers of fate and illness, adult and affair melodramas, the realist and healing romances of the 2010s, and music and arts melodramas last
secs: Hallyu Tearjerkers: Fate, First Love & Illness

leaves.label: Makjang Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean serial built on deliberately outrageous plotting: birth secrets, adultery, amnesia, chaebol family feuds and revenge escalating beyond plausibility (The Penthouse: War in Life, The World of the Married, East of Eden, Money Flower). A weekend family drama without the excess goes to B2-7.
leaves.see: B2-6 Revenge Drama; B2-7 Family Drama
leaves.axis: by the engine of the excess: birth-secret and family-feud serials first, then adultery and marriage makjang, then revenge and chaebol-intrigue makjang

leaves.label: Revenge Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean series whose spine is a protagonist's long-planned vengeance, usually wrapped in a romance or melodrama (Green Rose, Don't Look Back: The Legend of Orpheus, Goodbye Mr. Black, Call It Love). Revenge inside an outrageous family serial goes to B2-5 Makjang.
leaves.see: B2-5 Makjang Drama; B2-11 Thriller & Mystery Drama

leaves.label: Family Drama (gajok deurama)
leaves.defn: A Korean series centred on an extended family across generations, typically the long-running weekend family drama or the evening daily drama (My Golden Life, Young Lady and Gentleman, Homemade Love Story). Family serials driven by birth secrets and revenge go to B2-5 Makjang.
leaves.aliases: weekend drama (jumal deurama); daily drama (ilil deurama); home drama
leaves.see: B2-5 Makjang Drama; B2-4 Korean Melodrama

leaves.label: Sageuk (historical drama)
leaves.defn: A Korean historical drama set in the Joseon, Goryeo or Three Kingdoms periods, or a modern-era period drama of the Korean Empire, the colonial era and the later twentieth century (Jewel in the Palace, Jumong, Moon Embracing the Sun, Mr. Sunshine). A present-day romance with a brief slip into the past goes to B2-12.
leaves.aliases: sageuk; jeong-geuk (orthodox sageuk); fusion sageuk; daeha drama; sidae-geuk
leaves.see: B2-12 Fantasy Romance; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by mode, from historical fidelity to invention: orthodox jeong-geuk and dynastic epics first, then fusion sageuk of adventure, mystery and comedy, sageuk romance, fantasy, time-slip and horror sageuk, and modern-era period dramas last

leaves.label: Medical Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean series set among doctors and hospitals, whose cases and careers drive the story even when a romance runs alongside (Descendants of the Sun, Emergency Couple, Doctor Slump). A psychiatric healing melodrama goes to B2-4.
leaves.see: B2-2 Office Romance; B2-4 Korean Melodrama

leaves.label: Legal Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean series set among lawyers, prosecutors and judges, with cases framing the plot (I Hear Your Voice, Suspicious Partner, While You Were Sleeping). A Joseon-era lawyer goes to B2-8 Sageuk.
leaves.see: B2-9 Medical Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Thriller & Mystery Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean series driven by a crime, a mystery or a threat, usually entwined with a love story (The Smile Has Left Your Eyes, When the Phone Rings, The Trunk). A revenge plan as spine goes to B2-6; a police procedural without romance belongs in B7.
leaves.see: B2-6 Revenge Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Fantasy Romance
leaves.defn: A Korean romance series whose premise is supernatural or speculative: time slips, immortal beings (goblin, gumiho, grim reaper), body swaps, ghosts, superpowers or a fictional world (Guardian: The Lonely and Great God, My Love from the Star, Lovely Runner, W). A historical drama with fantasy elements goes to B2-8 section 4.
leaves.aliases: fantasy rom-com; time-slip drama; gumiho drama
leaves.see: B2-8 Sageuk; B9 Speculative Series
leaves.axis: by the supernatural device: time-slip, time-loop and reincarnation first, then mythical and immortal beings, body swaps and possession, ghosts and the afterlife, superpowers and science-fiction devices, and fictional or webtoon worlds last

leaves.label: School & Youth Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean series about teenagers or people in their early twenties, set in high school, university, idol training or sport, where growing up is the subject (Playful Kiss, Cheese in the Trap, Weightlifting Fairy Kim Bok-joo, Twenty-Five Twenty-One). A rich-heir high-school romance goes to B2-3.
leaves.aliases: teen drama; hakgyo drama; campus drama; cheongchun drama
leaves.see: B2-3 Chaebol Romance; B2-1 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by the youth setting: high school first, then university and twenty-something life, idol and music, and sport last

subs.label: Japanese Television Drama
subs.axis: Axis: by the genre or slot tradition Japanese broadcasting names: NHK serial forms first (asadora, taiga), then romance forms (trendy/getsuku, jun'ai, rom-com, office, school romance), then school, home and workplace dramas, gourmet and slice-of-life, and suspense and fantasy last

leaves.label: Asadora (Renzoku Terebi Shōsetsu)
leaves.defn: An NHK morning serial: some 150 fifteen-minute episodes over six months following a heroine's life, often across decades (Oshin, Amachan, Massan). A family drama in other slots goes to B3-9.
leaves.aliases: asadora; morning drama; renzoku terebi shosetsu
leaves.see: B3-2 Taiga Drama; B3-9 Home Drama

leaves.label: Taiga Drama
leaves.defn: NHK's year-long Sunday historical epic, one historical figure or era per year (Atsu Hime, Taira no Kiyomori, What Will You Do, Ieyasu?). Other period dramas belong in A8 or B1.
leaves.see: B3-1 Asadora; A8 Historical & Period Film

leaves.label: Trendy Drama & Getsuku
leaves.defn: A Japanese prime-time romance in the trendy-drama tradition: urban young professionals in love, star casts and theme songs, most famously Fuji TV's Monday 9 pm "getsuku" slot (Tokyo Love Story, Long Vacation, Beautiful Life, Rich Man, Poor Woman). A late-night or streaming romance goes to B3-4 or B3-5.
leaves.see: B3-4 Jun'ai & Romantic Melodrama; B3-5 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by phase of the cycle: bubble-era trendy dramas first, then the getsuku peak, then later getsuku and prime-time romances

leaves.label: Jun'ai & Romantic Melodrama
leaves.defn: A Japanese romance played for tears or for dark adult emotion: pure love against illness or death (jun'ai), forbidden or adulterous love (furin), obsessive love (Crying Out Love, in the Center of the World, Silent, Hirugao, Last Friends). A prime-time trendy romance goes to B3-3.
leaves.see: B3-3 Trendy Drama & Getsuku; B3-5 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by the obstacle to love: illness, death and pure love first, then adultery and forbidden love, then obsessive and dark romance

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy (ren'ai komedi)
leaves.defn: A Japanese romance series whose engine is comic: a contrived arrangement, a marriage hunt, a cohabitation or an oddball heroine, often adapted from josei or TL manga (Tokyo Tarareba Girls, Princess Jellyfish, Densha Otoko, Busu no Hitomi ni Koishiteru). An office love story goes to B3-6; a school romance goes to B3-7.
leaves.see: B3-6 Office Romance; B3-7 School Romance
leaves.axis: by the comic premise: contract and fake marriages first, then marriage-hunting and single life, cohabitation and housekeepers, makeovers and otaku heroines, rich-man Cinderella stories, and Teens' Love late-night romances last

leaves.label: Office Romance (shanai ren'ai)
leaves.defn: A Japanese romance set inside a company or workplace, between boss and subordinate or colleagues (Hotaru no Hikari, Oh My Boss! Love Not Included, Kissing the Ring Finger). A drama about the work itself goes to B3-10 Oshigoto Drama.
leaves.see: B3-10 Oshigoto Drama; B3-5 Romantic Comedy

leaves.label: School Romance (gakuen ren'ai)
leaves.defn: A Japanese romance among students, mostly live-action adaptations of shōjo manga, set in high school or college (Hana Yori Dango, Itazura na Kiss, Good Morning Call, Ao Haru Ride). A school drama about teachers, delinquents or clubs goes to B3-8.
leaves.see: B3-8 School Drama; B3-5 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by age and pairing: high-school romances first, then campus and young-adult romances, then teacher-student romances

leaves.label: School Drama (gakuen dorama)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series set in a school whose subject is the institution itself: the crusading teacher, the delinquent class, bullying, or the school club (GTO, Gokusen, The Queen's Classroom, Rookies). A love story between students goes to B3-7.
leaves.aliases: gakuen dorama; teacher drama; yankii drama; bukatsu drama
leaves.see: B3-7 School Romance; B10 Children's Series
leaves.axis: by the engine of the school story: teacher dramas first, then delinquent (yankii) dramas, bullying and dark classroom dramas, school-club and sports dramas, and school comedies last

leaves.label: Home Drama (hōmu dorama)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series about a household: siblings, parents and children, single fathers, a family's illness or hardship (Hitotsu Yane no Shita, Tonbi, One Liter of Tears, Mother). A comedy of everyday eccentricity goes to B3-12.
leaves.aliases: hōmu dorama; kazoku dorama; Showa home drama
leaves.see: B3-1 Asadora; B3-12 Slice-of-Life Drama
leaves.axis: by what tests the family: family ensembles first, then parenting and single parents, then illness, disability and hardship

leaves.label: Oshigoto Drama (workplace drama)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series about a job: the company, the trade, the profession or the industry is the subject (Naoki Hanzawa, Shomuni, The Pride of the Temp, Downtown Rocket). A romance at work goes to B3-6; a cooking or restaurant drama goes to B3-11.
leaves.aliases: oshigoto dorama; work drama; business drama
leaves.see: B3-6 Office Romance; B3-11 Gourmet Drama
leaves.axis: by the kind of work: corporate and finance first, then office comedies and temps, trades and service professions, media, publishing and entertainment, and medical, legal, care and rescue professions last

leaves.label: Gourmet Drama (gurume dorama)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series in which food, cooking and eating are the subject, often episodic around one dish per episode (Solitary Gourmet, Midnight Diner, The Makanai: Cooking for the Maiko House). A romance between cooks goes to B3-5 or B3-6.
leaves.aliases: gurume dorama; meshi-tero drama; food drama
leaves.see: B3-10 Oshigoto Drama; B3-12 Slice-of-Life Drama

leaves.label: Slice-of-Life Drama (nichijō)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series of everyday life with no strong romantic or professional engine: healing (iyashi) rhythms or eccentric small-group comedy (Yuru Camp, Barakamon, Kisarazu Cat's Eye, Tiger and Dragon). A food-centred series goes to B3-11.
leaves.see: B3-11 Gourmet Drama; C6 Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime
leaves.axis: by tone: healing (iyashi) slice of life first, then eccentric-ensemble comedy-drama

leaves.label: Suspense Drama (sasupensu)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series driven by a secret, crime or threat, often a domestic or romantic mystery (I Am Mita, Your Housekeeper, Quartet, Perfect Crime). A detective or police procedural belongs in B7.
leaves.see: B3-4 Jun'ai & Romantic Melodrama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Fantasy & Supernatural Drama
leaves.defn: A Japanese series whose premise is supernatural or science-fictional, usually framing a romance: a robot or alien lover, a ghost, a time slip, a body swap (Zettai Kareshi, Ima, Ai ni Yukimasu, Q10). Tokusatsu hero shows belong in B9.
leaves.aliases: fantasy romance; SF drama; tokusatsu-adjacent drama
leaves.see: B9 Speculative Series; B3-5 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by what the premise serves: fantasy-premise romances first, then supernatural and science-fiction dramas without a central romance
